title: Cluster Map from Points: See Point Patterns
description: Plot spreadsheet points and see their natural clusters with the Cluster Map from Points — patterns for stores, incidents or samples. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a delivery firm’s 800 drop points resolve into a handful of dense urban clusters and a long rural scatter — the map shows in seconds what the spreadsheet hid in rows.
quick_answer: The Cluster Map from Points plots a spreadsheet of coordinates on a map and groups nearby points into clusters you can read at a glance. Paste your points and watch the pattern emerge — dense cores, empty gaps and outliers — before committing to conclusions.
steps_intro: Rows hide geography. Clusters reveal it:

body.t: Customer points cluster where demand lives. Territories drawn around real clusters beat territories drawn around postcodes — start from a clean file via the
Calls, faults and sightings cluster for reasons — a hotspot map is the first exhibit in any ‘why here?’ investigation.
Field samples meant to spread evenly reveal their clumps on a cluster map. Fix the design before the fieldwork, not after.
The lone point 80 miles from its family is either a story or a typo. Clusters make loners impossible to miss.

At country zoom, a retailer’s points merge into a few regional blobs; zoom in and each blob splits into neighbourhood clusters. Both views are true — clustering is a scale-dependent reading, and the map lets you read at several scales.
A ring of clusters around an empty centre often means a lake, a park, a military range — or a data hole. The cluster map poses the question; local knowledge answers it.

popular_table.note: Clusters are visual groupings of your points — patterns in the data you supplied, computed in your browser. They describe the dataset first and the world only as far as the dataset does.

faq: Coordinate lists — typically latitude/longitude columns from a spreadsheet or CSV. Clean the file first (the coordinate validators here) and the clusters will be about geography, not typos.
By proximity on the map: points close together read as one cluster, separating as you zoom in. The grouping is a visual reading aid, not a statistical verdict.
How many points can I plot?
Browser plotting handles thousands comfortably; beyond that, aggregate first. A cluster map’s job is pattern-reading, and patterns saturate long before the browser does.
No — your file is read, not rewritten. Clusters exist only in this view.
The map is the analysis view. For cluster assignments as data, dedicated GIS or statistics tools export labels — this page gives you the pattern to specify them against.
Why do clusters merge when I zoom out?
Screen distance shrinks as zoom falls, so neighbours merge. It is the map’s honesty about scale, not instability — read patterns at the zoom of your decision.
A single isolated point is its own cluster of one — often the most interesting marker on the map.
